capabilities.target: Executive's calendar (accepts invites, drafts prep notes)
Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
Any recipient, from the executive's mailbox

inputs.source: Calendar invite, including from outside the company; description is free text written by the sender

instructions.note: 'find related documents' has no defined boundary, so the search can reach any document in the executive's drive, including board materials and draft financial results.
The agent treats any new invite, including from outside the company, as sufficient authority to trigger document search and an external email send, with no sender verification.

elements.name: Agent-generated daily summary of calendar and email actions

controls.name: Executive review of agent-generated daily summary
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is written by the same agent that performed the actions, after the actions already executed. A hijacked or more persuasive model can omit, understate, or mischaracterize what it sent (ASI09), and because it is after the fact it provides no preventive credit.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send with raw action review before external sends
Recipient allowlist for mail.send bound to a verified contact record, not to invite-controlled attendee fields
controls.decay_rationale: If recipients are restricted to a pre-verified contact list maintained outside the model's control, an uninvited external sender cannot appear as a valid destination, closing the exfiltration path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.search_and_read to exclude board and financial materials from invite-triggered flows
Treat invite free-text description as untrusted data that cannot steer document search or send scope
controls.decay_rationale: Structurally separating the invite's free-text fields from the decision of what to search and send narrows the path, but a sufficiently capable model may still find framing within the permitted fields (time, subject) that influences scope, so this control is not fully independent.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives confidential document read and irreversible external email send

attack_path.note: Anyone, including outside the company, can send an invite with a free-text description.
Agent auto-accepts the invite and begins the 'prepare' step on its own, with no approval.
Agent searches the executive's drive, which holds board materials and draft financial results.
Agent emails the brief, containing whatever it read, to the invite's attendees, with no recipient restriction.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version change increases the persuasiveness/completeness gap of self-written daily summaries, or the number of invites processed per day rises, with no approval gate or recipient allowlist added.

evidence.observation: The agent accepts any new invite and automatically searches documents and emails a brief in response, with no distinction between trusted and untrusted senders.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the invite description is free text written by the sender, so attacker-controlled content enters the agent's context directly.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, both highly sensitive and reachable by cap.drive_read.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so the brief can be sent to any attendee, including the invite's external sender.

recommendations.action: Require raw-action human approval before mail.send fires for any attendee outside a pre-verified internal contact list.
Restrict mail.send recipients to a verified contact record maintained outside model control, instead of the invite's attendee field.
Scope drive.search_and_read so board and financial materials are excluded from invite-triggered searches, or require a separate confirmation to include them.
Treat the invite's free-text description as untrusted data that cannot select which documents are searched or who receives the brief.

findings.title: Unbounded scope lets a trusted but ambiguous request reach restricted documents and an irreversible send

attack_path.note: Executive asks the agent to prepare for a meeting, without specifying which documents are relevant.
'Find related documents' has no defined boundary and can pull board or financial materials.
Brief is emailed to attendees with no recipient restriction and no approval step.

forecast.watch_signal: The agent's interpretation of 'related documents' widens over time, or new document sources are connected, with no scoping control or approval gate added.

evidence.observation: 'find related documents' has no defined scope, so a broad or ambiguous executive request can still pull in confidential or restricted material.
Drive includes board and financial materials, and mail.send has no recipient restrictions, so even a trusted, well-intentioned request can trigger an irreversible, high-sensitivity send.

recommendations.action: Apply the same credential scoping that excludes board/financial materials from automatic briefs regardless of whether the trigger is an invite or a direct executive request.
Define 'related documents' in the system prompt to exclude board and financial materials from automatic, unreviewed briefs.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted calendar invite (U) can, with no gate, drive a read of restricted board and financial materials followed by an irreversible external email send (S3), and the agent's unattended/unbounded step and runtime limits trigger the autonomy modifier. Residual stays critical because the design has no preventive controls at all on this path: no approval gate, no recipient allowlist, no credential scoping, and no separation of untrusted invite text from decision scope. The only control present, the daily summary, is detective, written by the same agent after the action completes, and behaviorally dependent (ASI09), so it earns no tier credit under the rubric. A second, lower-severity finding shows the same unscoped read-then-send path is also reachable from an ambiguous trusted request (moderate inherent, raised to high by the same autonomy modifier). Forecast equals residual for both findings: because the critical finding is already at the ceiling and no structural control exists to lose, model upgrades or longer task horizons mainly erode the one dependent control (the self-written summary), not the (absent) preventive layer. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a recipient allowlist bound to a verified contact record, independent of the invite's attendee field, which would sever the exfiltration path outright.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; the exact scope of drive.search_and_read, mail.send, and calendar.accept_and_prepare is inferred from prose descriptions, which limits confidence on precise credential scoping to medium.
The operator trust domain (first_party vs. third_party) was not stated in the artifacts and was not assumed.
